title: Horizontal Positioning Fixture Hydraulic Requirements
scope_statement: Validated scope: generic hydraulic component classes, functional valve behavior, and direct port-to-port connectivity only. Pump/cylinder/reservoir sizing, pressure and flow ratings, line selection, filtration, cooling, prime mover selection, simulation and fabrication approval are explicitly deferred to the later sizing and engineering phases.
design_narrative: Port-level topology for candidate_1 in repair mode. The valid open-circuit hydraulic power path is retained: Tank.S supplies Pump.S; Pump.P branches directly to ReliefValve.P and DCV.P; ReliefValve.T and DCV.T return directly to Tank.R. DCV.A and DCV.B connect through the selected dual pilot-operated check LoadLock to Cylinder.Cap and Cylinder.Rod. Advance is provisionally mapped to cylinder extension and return to cylinder retraction. No flow-control component is inserted because all speed decisions are sizing_only. The design remains blocked at selection/topology level for the reviewed safe-neutral holding requirement: the selected tandem-center DCV neutral unloads P to T but blocks A and B, so it cannot guarantee venting of valve-side pilot-release pressure for LoadLock reseating after command release.

function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Tank provides the open-circuit reservoir boundary with S connected to Pump.S as the suction source and R used as the common return sink for ReliefValve.T and DCV.T.

Pump is a fixed-displacement positive-displacement supply. Tank.S connects to Pump.S, and Pump.P branches directly to ReliefValve.P and DCV.P. Pump displacement and drive details are deferred to sizing.

ReliefValve is connected from Pump.P pressure branch to Tank.R through ReliefValve.P and ReliefValve.T. It provides topology-level overpressure protection and must be set/selected during sizing so maximum system pressure does not exceed 100 bar.

The selected tandem-center DCV provides commanded extend and retract states: extend connects P-A and B-T; retract connects P-B and A-T. Its neutral connects P-T with A and B blocked. It is the closest available catalog directional-control class but does not complete the safe-neutral pilot-vent repair.

LoadLock is installed between the DCV work ports and cylinder ports. A1/A2 serves the cap-side line and B1/B2 serves the rod-side line. It allows free flow from valve side to actuator side and blocks reverse flow from each chamber until the opposite valve-side work line is pressurized. Safe negligible-drift holding is contingent on pilot-release pressure being vented and the checks reseating in neutral; the selected DCV does not provide that vent path.

Cylinder provides powered bidirectional linear motion. Advance is provisionally mapped to extension with Cylinder.Cap pressurized through DCV.A and LoadLock.A1/A2, while Cylinder.Rod exhausts through LoadLock.B2/B1 and DCV.B/T. Return is provisionally mapped to retraction with Cylinder.Rod pressurized through DCV.B and LoadLock.B1/B2, while Cylinder.Cap exhausts through LoadLock.A2/A1 and DCV.A/T.

Advance and return numeric speeds are left to pump and cylinder sizing. No topology-level flow-control valve is added because the typed motion decisions specify sizing_only speed realization, no metering side, and no metered chamber or flow.

Not realized with the available catalog because no neutral A/B vent or separate pilot vent component is available. Command release must leave pilot-check reverse paths positively blocked; tandem-center A/B-blocked neutral can trap pilot-release pressure.

design_decisions.decision: Use only the selected runtime-catalog component set and direct port-level branching.
design_decisions.rationale: The final keys are limited to the supplied generic catalog metadata. Branching is represented by repeated endpoints such as Pump.P to ReliefValve.P and Pump.P to DCV.P. No manifold, tee, line, hose, filter, cooler, gauge, motor, coupling, shaft, electrical interface, or mechanical-drive interface is inserted.
driven_by: Runtime catalog was checked before selection; final keys are limited to generic classes returned by the catalog tools.
The open-circuit tank, fixed pump, relief valve, and no-flow-control decisions remain valid and are not regressed.

design_decisions.decision: Retain the open-circuit fixed-displacement pump and relief-valve power unit.
design_decisions.rationale: The tank supplies pump suction, the fixed pump supplies the pressure branch, and the relief valve diverts overpressure flow to tank. Relief setting is a sizing item constrained to the 100 bar maximum system pressure.
driven_by: The open-circuit tank, fixed pump, relief valve, and no-flow-control decisions remain valid and are not regressed.
No efficiency requirement exists; fixed-displacement pump is the simplest compatible catalog supply class.

design_decisions.decision: Retain the selected tandem-center 4/3 DCV only as the closest available catalog directional-control entry, not as a completed safety repair.
design_decisions.rationale: The selected DCV provides the required extend and retract paths for bidirectional cylinder motion, but its neutral state blocks A and B. That neutral cannot vent valve-side work and pilot-release volumes to tank for guaranteed LoadLock reseating after command release.
driven_by: The design-review fault is specifically neutral pilot-release pressure not being vented from the valve-side work lines feeding the pilot-check load lock.
The catalog contains no spring-centered 4/3 DCV whose neutral connects A and B to T; available 4/3 tandem and closed-center entries both block A and B in neutral.

design_decisions.decision: Retain the dual pilot-operated check LoadLock for the typed pilot_check holding decision, while recording the missing neutral vent path as blocking.
design_decisions.rationale: Negligible-drift holding cannot rely on DCV spool leakage alone. The selected dual pilot-operated check is the correct catalog class for static bidirectional load locking, but it requires release pressure to decay and the checks to reseat at neutral, which the selected tandem-center DCV does not ensure.
driven_by: The existing dual pilot-operated check remains the correct load-lock class for the typed pilot_check holding decision, but it requires the missing neutral vent/reseat path to be safety-acceptable.

Because no available catalog class can provide the required A/B venting neutral or a separate pilot-vent/reseat valve, the safety repair is blocked by a topology-class catalog gap rather than an executable replacement action.

design_decisions.decision: Do not add a flow-control valve.
design_decisions.rationale: The supplied motion decisions remain sizing_only for advance, hold, and return. Numeric speeds, forces, and stroke are pump/cylinder sizing requirements and do not justify a topology-level metering component.
driven_by: The open-circuit tank, fixed pump, relief valve, and no-flow-control decisions remain valid and are not regressed.
No flow-control valve is added because the supplied speed decisions remain sizing_only.

design_decisions.decision: Map carriage advance to cylinder extension and carriage return to cylinder retraction provisionally.
design_decisions.rationale: DCV.A is connected through LoadLock.A1/A2 to Cylinder.Cap, and DCV.B is connected through LoadLock.B1/B2 to Cylinder.Rod. This supports a complete phase definition while leaving final mechanical confirmation open.

Return provisionally mapped to retraction: pressurize Rod and return Cap.

catalog_gaps.capability: Spring-centered 4/3 directional valve neutral that vents both actuator work ports A and B to T for pilot-operated-check reseating, while still providing extend P-A/B-T and retract P-B/A-T states.
catalog_gaps.needed_component_class: 4/3 DCV with motor/float/open actuator-port center, or equivalent load-lock pilot-vent/reseat valve class
catalog_gaps.reason: Validation requires neutral to exhaust valve-side work and pilot-release volumes to tank. The catalog DCV classes are tandem-center with A and B blocked, closed-center with all ports blocked, and 4/2 with no neutral; none provides the required safe-neutral venting behavior.
catalog_gaps.chosen_workaround: No safe catalog workaround. Preserve valid components and block final repair until the missing class is added or an externally validated vent/reseat component is made available.

assumptions: Carriage advance corresponds to cylinder extension: DCV.A supplies LoadLock.A1/A2 and Cylinder.Cap during advance.
Carriage return corresponds to cylinder retraction: DCV.B supplies LoadLock.B1/B2 and Cylinder.Rod during return.
The horizontal carriage load is resistive and non-overrunning for topology selection; dynamic counterbalance load control is not required in the selected plan.
The dual pilot-operated check valve has internal cross-pilot release as described in the selected metadata, so no external pilot ports are available or required in the port-level topology.
Prime mover, electric wiring, filters, gauges, hoses, fittings, and manifolds are detail-design items outside this selected topology and are not instantiated.
Fixed-displacement pump drive details and displacement are deferred to sizing.
open_issues: Blocking: available catalog cannot implement the reviewed safe neutral for a pilot-check load-lock circuit because no DCV center vents A and B to tank and no separate pilot-vent/reseat valve class is available.
Confirm quantified negligible-drift tolerance and required hold duration for acceptance testing once the missing neutral-vent topology is available.
Confirm whether carriage advance corresponds to cylinder extension; swap A/B-to-cap/rod assignment if mechanical layout requires.
Sizing must verify 300 mm stroke, 15 kN advance load, 9.5 kN return load, required speeds, and relief setting at or below 100 bar.

The selected tandem-center DCV neutral connects P to T but blocks A and B. For the specified pilot-check load-lock circuit, command release must allow valve-side work/pilot-release pressure to decay so both pilot checks reseat and the actuator reverse paths are positively blocked. With A and B blocked, trapped pressure in the prior commanded work line can keep the opposite pilot check released, so safe neutral holding with negligible drift is not guaranteed. Use a 4/3 DCV neutral that vents A and B to T, or an equivalent validated pilot-vent/reseat topology.

The implementation is decomposed into subfunctions but does not provide a top-level function_implementation for position_carriage. That leaves the required advance, return, command-release neutral, and negligible-drift holding acceptance coverage incomplete at the required function level.

research_coverage.summary: Accumulated evidence is sufficient to design the requested hydraulic topology at the circuit-pattern level. The findings support an open-circuit power unit with reservoir, suction line, pump, pressure supply, pressure relief to tank, and return path; a double-acting cylinder driven by a spring-centered 4/3 directional valve; and a leak-resistant stopped/holding arrangement using pilot-operated check valves/load-holding valves in the cylinder lines with an appropriate center condition rather than relying on a closed-center spool alone. Critical safety cautions about spool leakage and uncontrolled motion are supported by real technical citations, and load-holding component classes and essential connection principles are identified.

items.rationale: Covered by textbook/technical citations supporting the essential open-circuit topology: reservoir to pump suction, pump outlet to pressure/supply line, control/actuator return to reservoir, and a pressure relief valve on the pressure side opening at a preset limit to return excess flow to tank. This is sufficient for a safe power and return path; exact pressure setting is a project sizing requirement rather than missing topology evidence.

Covered by citations supporting a double-acting cylinder controlled by a 4-way, 3-position directional-control valve, with P/T/A/B port roles, extension/retraction connection logic, and spring-centered return to neutral on command release. The findings also identify that neutral-center selection must be coordinated with the holding valves and not treated as the sole holding method where drift is unacceptable.

Covered by technical/manufacturer evidence that spool-type directional valves can leak and are not sufficient for positive holding, and that pilot-operated check valves in the cylinder lines with A/B ports connected to tank in neutral can keep a cylinder stopped. Additional safety evidence supports load-holding/counterbalance valves where uncontrolled or overrunning load motion is a concern, including placement in the actuator line and opposite-side pilot operation.

Covered by evidence for a leak-resistant load-holding topology: double/dual pilot-operated check valves or load-holding valves in the cylinder lines, cross-piloted from the opposite work line, with the directional valve centered to a safe neutral condition such as A/B to tank for POCV locking circuits. Manufacturer and technical citations state these valves are used for load holding, preventing drift/creep, and holding the cylinder/load when the pump or directional valve is neutral/off. Exact load capacity, pilot ratio, cracking pressure, and rated flow are component-sizing tasks rather than unresolved topology research.

missing_or_weak_information: Exact manufacturer part numbers, valve ratings, pilot ratios, relief setting tolerances, actuator bore/rod sizing, and hose/port sizes are not established by the research but are noncritical catalog/sizing decisions for the topology stage.

The ISO 4413 evidence is general safety-scope evidence, not a quoted actuator load-holding clause; however, the load-holding implementation itself is supported by multiple technical and manufacturer citations.

Actuator-port-mounted or close-coupled placement is best practice for minimizing unprotected hose volume, but the strongest extracted evidence only requires correct placement in the actuator/cylinder line; final detailed design should place holding valves as close to the actuator as practicable if hose-failure protection is required.

If the carriage can become an overrunning/gravity-assisted load rather than a purely resisted horizontal load, the designer should select a counterbalance/load-control valve topology or equivalent controlled-motion load-holding valve rather than relying only on pilot-operated checks for motion control.

design_issues.description: The selected tandem-center DCV neutral connects P to T but blocks A and B. For the specified pilot-check load-lock circuit, command release must allow valve-side work/pilot-release pressure to decay so both pilot checks reseat and the actuator reverse paths are positively blocked. With A and B blocked, trapped pressure in the prior commanded work line can keep the opposite pilot check released, so safe neutral holding with negligible drift is not guaranteed. Use a 4/3 DCV neutral that vents A and B to T, or an equivalent validated pilot-vent/reseat topology.

The topology records the missing A/B-to-T neutral or pilot-vent capability as a blocking catalog gap, but the deterministic report indicates that the requested generic capability already exists in the runtime catalog. This is not a valid CatalogGap; the functional repair should select the available safe-neutral DCV/equivalent rather than retain the known-unsuitable tandem-center DCV.

design_review.summary: Invalid. The open-circuit pump/tank/relief layout, extend/retract paths, actuator work-port load lock, and omission of flow controls are generally consistent with the brief.
